title: Per-token reward with a KL penalty against the SFT policy
goal:
In the RL step the environment is a bandit: the policy writes a whole response, the reward model scores it once, and the episode ends. The paper adds "a per-token KL penalty from the SFT model at each token to mitigate over-optimization of the reward model" (Section 3.5, Equation 2).

Write `token_rewards(logp_rl, logp_sft, rm_score, beta)`. The arrays `logp_rl` and `logp_sft` have shape `(T,)` and hold $\log\pi^{RL}_\phi(y_t \mid x, y_{<t})$ and $\log\pi^{SFT}(y_t \mid x, y_{<t})$ for the $T$ sampled tokens of one response. The float `rm_score` is $r_\theta(x, y)$. Return an array of shape `(T,)` with the reward for each token: $-\beta(\log\pi^{RL} - \log\pi^{SFT})$ at every token, plus `rm_score` at the final token only.

The reward model's scalar is paid once, at the end. Don't change the input arrays.
hints: The penalty uses the log of the ratio, so it is a difference of the two log-probabilities. Don't divide the probabilities and don't exponentiate.
A sampled-token log ratio can be negative. That is fine, and it makes the penalty a bonus on that token.
`rm_score` goes on `r[-1]` only. Put the penalty in a new array first (`-beta * (logp_rl - logp_sft)` creates one) so you don't write into the caller's arrays.
